raw_response:
My land is 9.2 mu and I've been working it for 20 years. I know this rotation — wheat goes in after the maize harvest in October, maize goes in after the wheat harvest in June. The whole 9.2 mu runs through both crops every year. That's just how we do it here in Quzhou.

I don't change much year to year because what I do works well enough. My neighbors use Jimai wheat varieties and Xianyu 335 or Zhengdan 958 maize — so do I. These seeds come from the township seed shop and I know they perform. I'm not going to try something unfamiliar on my whole field.

For fertilizer: I apply compound fertilizer at planting as a base, then top-dress urea on the wheat at jointing and on the maize around tasseling. I probably put on a bit more nitrogen than needed but that's how I've always done it — I'd rather not risk a thin crop when my family depends on this food and the little cash from selling extra.

Irrigation comes from the well. Wheat needs water in winter to protect roots from freezing, again at jointing, and again at heading. Maize I'll water at emergence if it's dry, and definitely at silking. I watch the sky and the crop — if the leaves curl, I irrigate.

For tillage I use the rotary tiller both times. It's cheaper to hire than a plough, faster, and gets the job done. We've been doing rotary for years.

Pesticide: I spray herbicide early on both crops, and usually one more time on the wheat for rust or aphids before heading. Maize gets a herbicide pass and sometimes an insecticide if I see stem borers.
